sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina National Adaptation Plan – NAP with proposed measures
sources.organization: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with UNDP and entity ministries
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate analysis through 2018, historical hazards, and projections through the end of the 21st century.
sources.methodology: Synthesizes climate records, sector studies and climate-model projections.
sources.limitations: The plan notes pending national analyses; proposed measures are not implementation evidence.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Floods, 2014: Recovery Needs Assessment
sources.organization: Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina with the European Union, United Nations and World Bank
sources.temporal_coverage: Assesses the 14–19 May 2014 floods and recovery needs identified by June 2014.
sources.methodology: Authorities, EU, UN and World Bank combined records, visits and rapid surveys.
sources.limitations: Findings use information available by June 2014.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Disaster Resilience Scorecard Assessment and Public Health Scorecard Addendum Analysis: Gaps, Challenges and Recommendations
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports local scorecards and DRR activities during 2021–2022.
sources.methodology: UNDRR analyzed municipal self-assessments and public-health scorecards.
sources.limitations: Selected local self-assessments, not an independent implementation evaluation.

sources.title: INFORM Subnational Risk Index for Bosnia and Herzegovina: Findings on natural hazard exposure, vulnerability and coping capacities, and recommendations for disaster risk management
sources.organization: United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security, guided by the European Commission Joint Research Centre INFORM methodology
sources.temporal_coverage: Municipal index published June 2026; includes historical disaster and war-legacy indicators.
sources.limitations: DRR capability and humanitarian coping indicators were excluded for insufficient data.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Floods Response – Multi-Cluster Initial Rapid Assessment
sources.organization: United Nations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, coordinated by the International Organization for Migration
sources.temporal_coverage: Rapid assessment of the 4 October 2024 storm, based on interviews conducted 2–6 November 2024.
sources.methodology: Light assessment based on 87 local key-informant interviews.
sources.limitations: Indicative sample; figures not independently verified.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 14–16, climate trends and locations repeatedly hit by extremes
claims.paraphrase: The NAP reports 1961–2018 warming (annual 0.4–1.2°C; growing-season up to 1.4°C), rising heavy-rainfall share and variability; it names Trebinje, Zenica, Laktaši and Sanski Most among repeatedly affected towns.
institutions: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 34, recent floods in the Sava Basin
claims.paraphrase: Record May 2014 rain plus snowmelt broke Sava embankments and flooded Central Posavina, Odžačka Posavina and Semberija; later heavy rain caused repeat flooding and landslides.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 41, modeled future peak streamflows
claims.paraphrase: Under RCP8.5, upper-quartile 100-year daily rainfall implies at least 23% higher end-century 100-year peak flows across modeled BiH Sava tributaries.
claims.scenario: RCP8.5; upper-quartile 100-year daily-rainfall value; end of the 21st century.
geographies: BiH tributaries of the Sava River Basin
institutions: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations
claims.limitations: Only Sava tributaries were modeled; no equivalent Adriatic-basin model was available.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 12–13, legislative and spatial-planning review
claims.paraphrase: In 2021, the NAP found climate law and spatial planning insufficient; environmental powers lay with the entities and Brčko, and existing plans had not integrated climate change.
claims.limitations: Dated institutional diagnostic; later reform status was not checked.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 13–14, Executive Summary: event and affected population
claims.paraphrase: After the May 2014 floods, 81 municipalities suffered impacts; about 90,000 people were displaced and more than 40,000 sheltered or stayed with relatives.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 15 and 253, Executive Summary and mine-action assessment
claims.paraphrase: Floods and landslides shifted mines/UXO from marked or suspected areas; 51 of 3,000 reported landslides were in suspected hazardous areas, and 105 km² was flagged as potentially contaminated.
institutions: Bosnia and Herzegovina Mine Action Centre
claims.limitations: Potential contamination estimate; site-by-site migration was uncertain.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The assessment links floods and landslides to movement of war-related explosives and a heightened civilian security threat.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 15 and 253–255, recovery needs and mine-action plan
claims.paraphrase: Residents in Posavina and Brčko reported mines/UXO near homes; repair and reconstruction in unsafe areas were restricted pending survey and clearance, leaving farmers and workers at risk.
institutions: Bosnia and Herzegovina Mine Action Centre
claims.limitations: The report describes planned recovery restrictions, not later implementation results.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Mine hazards required clearance before rebuilding infrastructure and returning affected land safely to communities.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 128, post-flood security response
claims.paraphrase: The RNA reports that Civil Protection and BHMAC response located and destroyed more than 10,000 mines, UXO and weapons, with no recorded casualties.
institutions: Bosnia and Herzegovina Mine Action Centre

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 4–6, 2021 city-level DRR platforms and measures
claims.paraphrase: Bihać, Bijeljina and Gradačac established local DRR platforms, adopted aligned strategies and risk assessments, and reported engineering measures and shock-responsive social-protection plans.
claims.limitations: Reported progress in three participating cities, not nationwide coverage.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 11–13, Busovača scorecard findings
claims.paraphrase: Busovača's scorecard names floods as its main hazard; it reports no training for poorest groups, recent business continuity plans in only 20–40% of firms, and warning reach of about half the population.
claims.limitations: Municipal self-scorecard; findings were not independently measured.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 17–18, Jajce scorecard findings
claims.paraphrase: Jajce reports an outdated risk assessment, no training for poorest groups, continuity plans in under 20% of firms and warning reach below half the population.
claims.limitations: Municipal self-scorecard; findings were not independently measured.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 8–9, hazard exposure hotspots and Konjic population
claims.paraphrase: INFORM ranks Brod (7.5) and Bihać (7.3) highest for exposure; Neretva municipalities Konjic and Mostar face flood/landslide risks, and about 12,000 people in Konjic live in landslide-prone areas.
institutions: United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security
claims.limitations: Composite exposure scores are relative and do not capture every local event.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 8–9, Jablanica 2024 event and index score
claims.paraphrase: The report records a 2024 Jablanica landslide that buried buildings and killed 19 people, although its municipal hazard-exposure score was moderate.
claims.limitations: The index is a comparative municipal model, not an event-warning tool.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 10–11, vulnerability and disaster recovery drivers
claims.paraphrase: Trnovo (RS) and Foča score 7.4 for vulnerability with unemployment above 20%; the report links job scarcity partly to war-damaged economies and says benefit dependence hampers post-disaster recovery.
claims.limitations: Model-based account of selected vulnerability drivers.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report links post-war destruction of businesses and infrastructure to job scarcity, and benefit dependence to weaker recovery after disasters.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 12–13, local coping-capacity drivers
claims.paraphrase: Bosansko Grahovo, Livno and Kupres score poorly on coping capacity; Bosansko Grahovo's road density is under one-seventh the national average, constraining evacuation and aid access.
claims.limitations: Indicators draw on available public datasets.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 2 and 7–8, overview and Jablanica profile
claims.paraphrase: The rapid assessment says road and bridge damage restricted movement from remote areas and slowed recovery; in Jablanica it counted 483 affected people and 188 evacuees across interviewed flood-hit locations.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 6–7, UN Women gender perspective overview
claims.paraphrase: The report warns GBV could rise after flood-related livelihood loss, overcrowding and distress; disrupted services may also hinder survivor reporting.
claims.scenario: Conditional post-flood humanitarian risk; no incidence estimate or time window is stated.
geographies: flood-affected areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina
claims.limitations: Anticipated risk; no measured increase; cites UN Women rapid report.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links livelihood loss, crowding and distress to possible GBV, and service disruption to underreporting.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 5–6, gender and social-protection needs
claims.paraphrase: The assessment calls for mobile maternal, reproductive and psychological care for women and girls in remote areas; it names social-care staffing shortages in Jablanica, Konjic and Kiseljak.
claims.limitations: Rapid needs assessment, not service-coverage evaluation.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 3–4, support during the first four weeks
claims.paraphrase: Responders reported aid across six affected municipalities; civil protection, governments, UN/NGOs, businesses and community groups coordinated food, water, medicine, cash and repair kits.
claims.limitations: Assistance reported for the first four weeks; outcomes were not evaluated.

access_audit.notes: Opened the complete public 168-page NAP and inspected climate trends, local floods, modeled streamflows and institutional review.

access_audit.locator: One-based PDF pp. 13–15 and 128, 253–255; executive-summary methodology and mine-action passages
access_audit.notes: Opened the complete public 302-page assessment and read the affected-population, hazard/war-remnant interaction and recovery passages.

access_audit.locator: PDF cover/printed pp. ii–vi; one-based PDF pp. 6, 11–13 and 17–18 for platforms and municipal scorecards
access_audit.notes: Opened the complete public 40-page report; reviewed methodology and the cited municipal self-assessment passages.
access_audit.reuse_terms: PDF says it may be freely quoted with acknowledgment; license_status left unknown.

access_audit.locator: One-based PDF pp. 3–13; methodology, exposure hotspots, vulnerability, coping-capacity and risk findings
access_audit.notes: Opened the complete public 27-page June 2026 municipal risk-index report.

access_audit.locator: One-based PDF pp. 1–8 and 19–20; Jablanica profile, gender analysis, response and methodology/limitations
access_audit.notes: Opened the complete public 21-page rapid assessment and checked its key-informant sample, scope and limitations.

search_audit.query: Bosnia and Herzegovina named municipal flood drought landslide vulnerability groups climate reports subnational
search_audit.outcome: Read the NAP, 2026 INFORM municipal report, 2014 recovery assessment and 2024 MIRA for named locations, groups and differentiated exposure/coping capacity.

search_audit.query: Bosnia climate change conflict security landmines floods gender-based violence social tension primary reports
search_audit.outcome: Found source-stated flood/landslide displacement of war-era mines/UXO and a conditional post-flood GBV risk; no inspected source establishes climate-driven armed or intercommunal violence.

search_audit.query: Bosnia postwar mines conflict legacy constrain flood recovery reconstruction climate adaptation official assessment
search_audit.outcome: The RNA states mine/UXO clearance restricted rebuilding and kept land workers at risk; INFORM links post-war economic destruction to job scarcity and weaker recovery. No inspected source documented ongoing armed violence interrupting adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Bosnia Herzegovina local disaster resilience capacity early warning social protection flood scorecard 2026 INFORM
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed local DRR platforms and municipal warning/training gaps, 2026 coping-capacity contrasts, and 2024 response coordination; coverage is selected-site or rapid-assessment evidence.

gaps: No inspected primary source establishes current armed or intercommunal violence disrupting adaptation or disaster-risk-reduction delivery. The clearest conflict interaction is legacy mine/UXO contamination affecting flood recovery; INFORM also documents war-related economic scarring and weaker disaster recovery.
The 2021 NAP is a dated institutional baseline; later legal and spatial-planning reforms were not verified. Its Sava flood model does not cover the Adriatic watershed.
The 2026 INFORM index excludes disaster-risk-reduction capability and humanitarian coping indicators because of insufficient data; its composite rankings are not event warnings.

The UNDRR municipal scorecards are selected local self-assessments from 2021–2022, and the 2024 MIRA is a purposive key-informant snapshot rather than a representative or independently verified post-disaster assessment.
The MIRA GBV statement is a conditional risk attributed to a separate UN Women rapid gender report; this collection did not independently inspect that separate report.
